title: TUA-Bench: Benchmarking General-Purpose Terminal Agents
hook: 120 real terminal tasks — from email triage to PhD-level scientific workflows — show even Claude Opus 4.8 tops out around 66%, far from reliable general computer use.
key_points: Existing benchmarks split badly: GUI benchmarks skip terminals, and terminal benchmarks focus almost entirely on coding.
TUA-Bench adds 120 real-world terminal tasks across five families, including document editing, email, and PhD-level scientific workflows.
Each task runs in a real terminal with deterministic setup and execution-based scoring.
The best frontier agent (Claude Code, Opus 4.8, max reasoning) scores 65.8% overall — with large gaps across tracks.
content_html: Coding agents already live in the terminal, but most benchmarks judge them only on shell scripting and programming tasks. TUA-Bench asks a broader question: can an agent use the terminal the way a person handling everyday digital work — and even specialized science — actually would?
extra_html: The gap TUA-Bench fills is real: general computer-use benchmarks mostly target graphical interfaces, while terminal benchmarks lean almost entirely on programming-centric shell workflows. TUA-Bench instead introduces 120 manually designed, real-world tasks across five task families — routine activities like document editing, email management, and live-web information seeking, plus scientific and engineering workflows co-designed with PhD-level domain experts requiring specialized software. Every task runs in a real terminal with a deterministic setup script and execution-based scoring. Even the strongest agent tested, Claude Code running Claude Opus 4.8 at maximum reasoning effort, reaches only 65.8% overall, with substantial gaps between task tracks — a sign that general-purpose terminal competence is still an open problem, not a solved one. Shoufa Chen and colleagues, arXiv 2026.
